utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: I do remember. I was wearing the tracksuit pants and top and also a blazer, a black blazer, and I also had yellow training shoes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What colour was your hair at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: The same as it is now. I had the same hairstyle and the same hair colour. I always have the same hairstyle.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How long was your hair on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Perhaps a centimetre or two longer than it is right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you agree that your hair is touching your shoulders at the moment, you have blond straight hair touching your shoulders when you sit back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How far away from your apartment was the other place where you baked the bread, where you went to bake the bread?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Perhaps 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And did you in fact go there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At some stage later, did your husband arrive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes, my husband came. He had been listening to the radio. I have to say that it was powered by a car battery. He somehow managed to get it hooked to the car battery and he was listening to the news and he told me, leave the bread behind, leave everything. There is a message from Karadzic that Sarajevo would be shelled, as that day a convoy of Serbs was supposed to leave Sarajevo and our authorities would not allow it to go because the Serbs would not let the humanitarian aid go through Ilidza. My husband came immediately and said: "Leave everything behind. Let's go home because Sarajevo is about to be shelled." Of course, that is exactly what I did. I came together with my neighbour. We didn't wait for the bread to be finished. We just went back to our apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So your husband told you what he had heard on the radio; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You said that he heard that Mr. Karadzic said that Sarajevo would be shelled because a convoy of Serbs had not been allowed to leave Sarajevo --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes, that he would "raze Sarajevo to the ground." That is a verbatim quote.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You also said that the reason the authorities would not allow the convoy to leave Sarajevo is because the Serbs, and I now quote your words as translated into English, "because the Serbs would not let the humanitarian aid go through Ilidza." Do you mean by that the Serbs would not let some humanitarian aid come into the city through Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So did you leave -- you said that you went back to your apartment. Did your neighbour leave with you to return to the apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What happened after that? Was there any shelling that you saw or heard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: No. Quite the contrary. It was uncommonly quiet. There wasn't a single shot to be heard and I decided to go back for the bread because I had left the bread behind to bake. And the family where I baked the bread, they didn't have any dishwashing liquid and I took some as a present for them. I also took the bread. I was carrying it like this, together with the metal pan in which it was. When I was about halfway there, I suddenly heard the shots. At the same time, the bread fell out of my hands and I felt the blood on my left side. Although the bullets entered one centimetre away from my spine and passed right through my body and exited the left side of my body creating a huge exit wound and rupturing the artery. I managed to make a few more steps and seek shelter behind one of the neighbouring skyscrapers. I fell down and, of course, I wanted to ask for help but there was nobody in the street because everybody had taken shelter in light of the information that was received over the radio. So I didn't know what to do, how to seek help. And the easiest thing was to shout as loud as I could. Since this was a skyscraper full of people, I was hoping that somebody would come down and pick me up. I screamed once, waited for a very short period of time, and then I screamed again. But when I wanted to scream for the third time, I didn't have the strength to do it. Of course, I was already losing consciousness, but I felt a shadow that grabbed me. Somebody had heard me. A person grabbed me by the caller and was asking somebody else for help. It was a young man, later I learned that after I left the hospital, whose name was Srdan. He was the first person to come to my aid. He is a Serb. They picked me up and took me to the first aid station which was maybe 50 metres away from that area. Of course, I was immediately transported from the first aid point to the hospital. I was naturally unconscious, but I was taken to the hospital where I was immediately transferred to the operation room, where I received 17 bottles of blood because I arrived in the hospital clinically dead, without a pulse. So they gave me 11 units of blood on the operating table and they tried to by-pass the artery that had been ruptured. When they did all that and when they wanted to get me off the table, it ruptured again. So I had to be taken back to the operating theater. Of course, this is what I heard later. They made another incision in my stomach and again they by-passed this part of the artery that was ruptured. I spent 23 days in the intensive care. But as you can see, I survived.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will now go back over the account that you have just given us and ask you some further questions about it. Earlier on you said that you were carrying the bread pan like this, and when you said those words, you were holding the bread pan on your right side, I think in the area of your hip; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes, on the right side, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You said that the bullet left your body on the left side and you felt blood on the left side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes, that is right, on the left side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: It was actually gushing. The blood was gushing because the artery had been ruptured.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there any damage done to the bread pan? Was that hit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At about the time that you were shot, did you hear the sound of a shot being fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes, I heard the sound. At the same time, I dropped pan at the same time and I felt the blood. It was all -- it all happened in a single moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: From what --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Virtually simultaneously. That is when I heard the shots and felt the blood.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: From what direction did you hear the sound of the shot come?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: From behind my back and that was from the direction of Grbavica. That location is very close to Grbavica. In fact, there is only one road and the river of Miljacka between that part of the city and Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you say that the sound of the shot seemed to come from behind your back, do you mean by that directly behind your back or slightly to the left or slightly to the right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Not directly from behind my back, but slightly to the right because that is where the bullet entered my body. So slightly to the right, not directly from behind my back.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: To your right, how far was the front line approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: I don't know. 50 to 100 metres. Not more than that. Well, the width of the road, I don't know how wide it is, and then you also have the river. They were on the other side of the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think you have said that the -- I will withdraw that. What was the name of the area on the other side of the river closest to where you were? What part of Sarajevo was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: On the other side of the river?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In that part of Grbavica, were there any high-rise buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What were those buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: There was the shopping, two yellow buildings that were called "Shopping by Us," and there were four white skyscrapers. And from these four white skyscrapers and the two shopping buildings, you can see the spot where I was wounded quite clearly, practically with the naked eye. In fact, not practically, but you really see it. If you look at that point from the shopping buildings or the white skyscrapers, you can see the people quite clearly because the distance is very small.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Approximately how far were you from where you lived at the time that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: From the place where I was shot? Maybe 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Given that you lived so close and that you lived there up until that time, had you developed any awareness of whether there was sniping fire coming from the shopping buildings or any of the four other high-rise buildings that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: We all knew it. I wasn't the only person to be wounded. Many people were killed. In fact, from the shots fired from the shopping buildings and the skyscrapers, the white skyscrapers, quite a few people who lived in my street were killed or wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, you said that you went to this other place with your neighbour to bake some bread. Your husband arrived and warned you to leave, so you and your husband and the neighbour, I think, went back to where you lived; is that correct? You returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes, yes, to our apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: There was no shelling and so you decided to go back again; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes, to take -- to collect the bread.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And to take some detergent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you shot on the way the second time to this other place or were you shot after you collected your bread and dropped off the detergent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: After I collected the bread.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So you were returning to your apartment the second time when you were shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, you told us it was very quiet, I think you said something like unusually quiet, strangely quiet --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- and then you heard the sound of the shot. Did you hear any other shooting before you lost consciousness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us that the wound left a large or a significant injury on your left-hand side. Did the doctor say anything to you about how big the hole was created by the bullet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes. My surgeon who performed surgery on me told me that -- he said verbatim, "I put both of my hands," and these are a man's hands, "into your exit wound." That is how large it was and he showed like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, when you finally left the hospital, were you given some documents by the hospital staff in relation to your admission and treatment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, I was given such documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask the witness be shown Exhibit P3282. I don't ask that it be placed on the ELMO because it contains features which would allow for the witness's identification. So perhaps you could just look at it. It might assist -- I withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President I am waiting to be able to check the number of the document which is not -- doesn't seem to be complete. But that doesn't matter. What we wanted to say, Your Honour, Mr. President, is the following and we will say that at a later date because we don't want to interrupt the testimony of the witness, and that is that these documents in their entirety have finally been submitted to the Defence in the form which is more or less legible. I don't know exactly when it was at what time, but we do know what day it was, it was yesterday. I have to say that last night, to be more specific, so yet again the Defence is handicapped to a quite large extent in the preparation of our work because we cannot keep on cross-examining the witnesses on the run and that is exactly what is required -- what we are required to do. If you compare the quality of these documents with the documents that we received before it cannot be compared, really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has received this morning the complaint about legibility you filed, I think, yesterday and I do see that there is a difference. Let's see how far we can come and let's just establish that it is not a good thing that you received the better readable copies only recently, but at the other hand, be glad that we have them at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just two things very briefly. Firstly, the reason the Defence received those copies yesterday is that we received them for the first time yesterday. The witness kindly brought those documents with her. Secondly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The better legible ones, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Secondly, as I have said before, the Prosecution does not particularly rely on these types of documents in these types of situations. I intend to tender only the first two pages of P3282. The purpose being it is some corroboration of what the witness has already said. I do not intend to tender any of the other medical documentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is clear at least. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Madam, would you please look at the photocopies in front of you. Do you recognise those pages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are they some of the documents that you have received from the medical authorities in relation to your treatment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Might that be returned. Mr. President, at this stage, I propose to show the witness a photograph and shortly after a video taken in the usual fashion for these types of matters, and as well as that, a 360-degree photograph and a map. The details in those four items would permit to a greater or lesser degree some identification of either the witness or where she lived at the time. Therefore, I would be grateful if we can go into closed session for the next phase of examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have been informed that the witness -- the video could reveal information which is protected so therefore we turn into private session or closed session? Which would you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the photograph and the map will also allow identification and probably answers to the questions asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will then turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes it is confirmed to my screen. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us that when you were shot, there was no one around and you called out, hoping that someone in the high-rise buildings near you would hear you and come to your assistance. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were there any military weapons or equipment anywhere near you at the time that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Then we'll have a break. Who is going to cross-examine the witness after the break? Will it be you, Ms. Pilipovic or Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence does not know yet. We did not have time to go through these medical documents that were given to us very late, but we will consult each -- I will consult my colleague. Do you have a preference? It's either myself or my colleague, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't have a preference. I was just trying to see what situation we are in. It is now Thursday. We are not sitting on Friday. The examination-in-chief took one hour. If we would have a break until 10 minutes to 1.00, there would be 55 minutes left for cross-examination until we have to finish. If it would be possible to conclude the cross-examination at that time, that would mean the witness could presumably travel back home and didn't have to wait.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am terribly sorry. Independently of whether it is myself or my colleague, we shall attempt to be brief, as long as we are not interrupted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will have a break until 10 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, we urge the Defence to finish in time so... Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I will raise an issue at this point. It does not really matter if the witness is in the courtroom or not. But the Defence wishes indicate that we are opposing to -- we have an opposition. These documents were -- these medical documents that I do not have right here under my eyes, it is P3283, was tendered by the Prosecution. When we compare these documents as being relatively legible documents but they are not all completely legible. These documents have nothing to do with the document delivered to the Prosecution, which were submitted in the month of December of 2001. So when we are submitted something that is called a "black box," I must say that one does not accomplish the communication duty or obligation. It is only last night that we have received these documents and if the legislator desired that some delay passed by between the moment that the Defence for instance receives the documents and before they start cross-examining, it is obvious that every time, if these delays are not respected, and each time if these documents are submitted to us at the very last moment, I must say that it is not tolerable, it is not acceptable and it is not abiding by the Rule on behalf of the Prosecution. This is why we would like to raise a fundamental objection. We cannot use the documents because they were not disclosed pursuant to the Article 65 ter of the Rules and regulation. This is what I wanted to say very briefly. I wished to be brief and therefore this is why we are going to do two things, if you allow us, Mr. President. Ms. Pilipovic will begin the cross-examination of this witness and then I will only ask some final questions regarding these documents. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, first of all, I apologise for being late. There were some trial team matters that I attended to and it took me a little longer than I anticipated and I should have been watching the time more carefully. Do you wish to hear from me in relation to what Mr. Piletta-Zanin has said or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact I would rather first start with the cross-examine of the witness, for reasons known to all of us. But if you would just grant me one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please confirm that on the 25th of June, 2001, you spoke to the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of the examination-in-chief, you told us that the incident in which you were hurt occurred on the 7th of November, 1992. Can you please tell us from the time when the incident occurred as you described to us and up until the time when you gave the statement to the investigators, that would be the 25th of June, 2001, so in that intervening period, did you speak to anyone about the incident in which you were injured or did you report the incident to anyone? I am referring to the incident which you were wounded on the 7th of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to gain some time, perhaps it would be good for the witness to reply into the microphone. It would be good to have two microphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are not aware, but could you just adjust the microphones to such a way, Mr. Usher, so that we can clearly hear the witness. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So, Witness, you do confirm for the first time after November, 1992, you spoke to the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor on the 25th of June, 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you spoke to the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor on that day, were you shown the medical documents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When the medical documents were shown to you by the investigator who interviewed you, did you say that you recognised the documents that you considered to be yours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you say to the investigators that you had the originals of the documents and did you in fact have them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you supply these documents to the investigators on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: The documents that the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor showed you, were these copies or the originals from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: I don't really remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you inspected the documents shown to you by my learned colleague today, the documents that you inspected in June 2001, were they the same as the documents that you inspected today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember. I didn't pay that much attention. I saw that the documents shown to me today were photocopy. And on that occasion, on the previous occasion, I didn't pay much attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I will now read a part of your statement given on the 25th of June, 2001 and I will read on page three where you said that you inspected -- that you inspected documents 0098359, 00983361 -- and 00983361. You go on to say, "I recognise them as copies of the original medical documents. I have been given in relation to my injury."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember what it looked like. I probably saw it at that time and that is why I stated it that way. I assumed that it is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the ERN numbers read out my by my friend are different from those who appear in the statement. The numbers which appear in the statement are 00983359, 00983360 and 00983361. I don't require any changes be made to the questions that was put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you do confirm that the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor showed you the documents that you recognised as copies of the documents bearing your full name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, in the course of your examination-in-chief, you told us where you lived. You said that the front lines were 50 metres away from where you were. When you say "50 metres away" --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: I said between 50 and 100 metres. I am not quite sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what -- which army was located at the distance of about 50 to 100 metres way from the buildings that you lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: From the buildings where I lived?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: I don't know what army it was because I didn't see any troops.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this question. In the area where you lived, did you see any soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Well, from time to time I would encounter somebody as I went to work, somebody wearing a uniform, but whether that person was a soldier or whether he wore a uniform of some sort, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You had work obligation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement - I will not now say the name of the company to protect you - the company where you worked under the work obligation, how far was that company from the place where you lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Perhaps 2 to 3 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In 1992, do you have any knowledge whether the headquarters of the BH army was also located in the company where you worked, in the building where you worked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: No, I am absolutely sure that there wasn't anything such thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In the building where you lived or parallel to it, is there the Energoinvest building block?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether in 1992 and 1993 and 1994 that the headquarters of the 102 Motorised Brigade of the BH army headquarters was located there in the Energoinvest building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: I did not see any soldiers next to the building of Energoinvest when I went to work, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm to us that street where you lived goes parallel to the Zmaja od Bosne Street, used to be Marshal Tito Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And that parallel to the Zmaja od Bosne Street and parallel to the Miljacka river, there is a section of the part of the city and buildings that are called Wilsonovo Setaliste, the promenade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, parallel to the street where you live, and in relation to the Marshal Tito Street, which buildings are there in the area of the Wilson promenade facing the Miljacka river?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: I don't know how to explain to you which buildings there are. I know that there are some buildings but I don't know how you want me to explain this.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So parallel to the street where you live, is there the Bristol Hotel quite near?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes, quite near, but it is not on the Wilson promenade.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In this area that is parallel to your street, is there the building of the school for electrical engineering, the faculty of electrical engineering?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: No, it is not on that street. It is further towards the -- the Wilson promenade, but it is not the electrical engineering, but the mechanical engineering faculty.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: From the building or from the floor where you lived and from the area where your street is, were you able to see those buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: No. Because in front of my building there was a building that closed off the line of sight. It is possible perhaps to see from the upper floors, but I was unable to see those buildings from my floor because the building that is located in front of my skyscraper high-rise building is, I think, eight floors high so I was unable to see.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: The buildings that were parallel to your street in the part of the Wilson promenade, were they parallel to the skyscrapers in Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: There were some skyscrapers in Grbavica which were parallel but not the ones that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How many skyscrapers there are on Grbavica, as far as you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: I don't know, really. I never counted them.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to see from your street the four skyscrapers in Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: The four skyscrapers below the bridge, the Brotherhood and Unity Bridge, I couldn't see them from my skyscraper, but I could see them from my street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In the period in the years of 1992, 1993, and 1994, did you go to the area parallel to your street that is called the Wilson promenade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: In the course of the war, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that in that area there were the positions of the 102nd Motorised Brigade and that the BH army was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: No. Believe me, I really don't know. I wasn't really interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In the street where you lived, was there the Vase Miskina company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How far away is that company from the building where you lived or the buildings where you were at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: It was very close. Perhaps some 50 metres, 20, 30, something like that. Not more than 50.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge that, from June onwards, that the staff of the Territorial Defence, and later on the headquarters of the 102nd Motorised Brigade, the command post of that brigade was located in that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: No. Well, I am not a soldier and I was not really preoccupied with that. I just ran from home to work, from work to home, and that was it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that the witness was -- testified in front of this Tribunal and that he testified that the staff of the Territorial Defence and that the headquarters of the 102nd brigade was located there, would you agree with me that it is possible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: I swore that I would speak the truth and I am speaking the truth. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object. The question has no probative value given the previous answer of the witness. If she doesn't know, she can't comment

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is sustained.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, on that day when you said the incident happened, in the area where you were as you showed us on the video, were there any other persons there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: No. There was nobody there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement that you gave to the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor, you said that you noticed a person in sight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: No, that is not what I said. I said I saw a silhouette, a shadow Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. of a person. That was the young man that picked me up. I didn't see anybody there at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In 1992, 1993, and 1994, in the part of the city where you lived, were there any combat operations going on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: You mean direct combat operations there? I don't know about that. There were -- there was shelling. People were being wounded, but I did not see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this concludes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Pilipovic. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, madam, and thank you for coming here. I will ask you questions in French. I will be brief so that you can go back home for the weekend. Witness, you said that during the course of the summer 2001, you were interviewed by the members of the OTP. Is that correct? You confirmed this fact.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. You also said that you have shown some -- you were shown some medical documents which you recognise as being documents relating to your injuries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, thank you. I would like to show you now a document bearing the ERN number, but first of all, I would like to ask you the following question: Do you speak and do you understand the French language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am asking you this because of one precise issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like the witness to be able to, although if she doesn't understand English --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you speak English?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would nevertheless ask the witness to remove her headphones for just one second because there is something that I would like to say. Thank you, Mr. President. The problem is the following, and I will say it very openly. I would like to show the witness now a document. It is document bearing mark 5958 in its version such as we have received it the day before yesterday. I would like to ask her a series of questions regarding this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Prior to clarifying one thing: Mr. Ierace, it was my understanding that you tender P3282, but only the first two pages. Or do you tender the whole document and you are only examining the witness on the first two page?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The former, Mr. President. The first two pages and the relevant transcript for the first two pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Translation. I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So therefore, when we finally deal with the documents, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you should be aware that only the first two pages are tendered. It might perhaps have been wiser only to give the first two pages if you intended not to tender the other two pages. But getting rid of paper is easy.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the questions that I will ask stem out of the interview that occurred in June of 2001, and this is why it is important that we know how and under which circumstances it all occurred. This is why I will ask questions only regarding the first two pages. May I proceed? These documents are an annex of the motion that you've received this morning and that we have also received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was responding. Since you referred to 5958, which is not the first two pages. That is the reason why I responded. Because the first two pages is 5556. But please proceed because you always could tender them yourself if the Prosecution doesn't do it. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was talking about 5958. We can ask the witness maybe to put back her headphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam, would you please put on your headphones? Thank you very much. The witness [sic] will show you, Witness, with his kind assistance, a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Usher, would you kindly show this to the witness. No, it's the one I have in my hand. For the transcript, we are talking about the document 0211-5958, which was annexed to the motion filed before you, Mr. President. Filed to your Chamber, in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you give me one moment. You might have noticed some activity from the usher. That was because I would like to have in front of me your submission of yesterday. I hope we found it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to try to not waste time, so may I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your question to the witness was whether she can read her name on that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If she was able to make out a name that is on the document handed to her.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Could we also see the copy that has been presented to the witness at this very moment so that we could compare it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I compared it with the filed submission "determination de la defense a redaction a la problematique des pieces illisibles." Do you have that as well, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I don't have it in front of me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please show it briefly to Mr. Ierace and return it back to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I now have that and I take it that was attached to the submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I checked that. Yes, if it would then please be --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask Mr. Ierace not to write anything on the document, and to give it back to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you have stated a few moments ago that you were not able to make out your name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps I can short-circuit this. Mr. President, I hand up to you the copies from the evidence folder these documents. It makes clear that why these ERN numbers ending in 957 and 958 are in the condition in which they appear in the photocopies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is the originals you are producing now?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. I have a stamp and a signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, that is not the most important thing right now. I believe that it would be better to cross-examine this witness at this very moment. And if they are talking about documents that were not handed out to us, later on the Defence will make another objection and maybe the witness will then have to come back on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar. Mr. Usher, would you show it briefly to Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Please proceed with your cross-examination, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you stated earlier that you were not able to read a name, any name on this document; do you confirm this fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, isn't it true to say that this document seems to be mainly legible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes, quite illegible [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Is this a type of document that the Prosecution showed you and that you would have supposedly recognised as being your own documents in June of 2001 during your interview?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: I said that I do not recall what the documents looked like. I remember the first part which is on the paper. I said those are these documents. I can see approximately from what we can read that it is the same document that I was issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam, were you shown at the time a document that was so illegible, because we cannot even see your name and we don't even know what the object of this document is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: I said that I do not remember what these documents look like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I have a question to you. As far as your understanding goes, is 5958 the back side of 5957? I specifically asked you to look at the right-hand bottom corner of 5958 and to the left-hand bottom corner of 5957.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I do not have the document before me any longer. I would have to be able to see it again, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You refer to the documents attached to your submission and these are both attached to your submission.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, most likely there is a transparency problem with regards to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand. But if there is a fair possibility that this is the back side and --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that was the very reason that I handed up the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When one has a look at this document which is from where the photocopies are made, it is quite clear that 5958 is not only the reverse of 5957, but it is obvious that one is seeing through either side the printing on the reverse. In other words, the questioning has no probative value. For this reason the name clearly wouldn't be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's just see whether we can complete this. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, after you have the document number 5957 in front of you, because what I want is to avoid confusion and to promote clarity. Would you please present to the witness number 5957 and you may do it in the old, bad, legible copy. If you haven't got one, I have one for you here, and ask the witness whether she can read any name on that document which...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am looking for this document ending with 57. I do not know if I have it here. I see 56.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the time being, I could give you the copies you attached originally to your submission file.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gladly, Mr. President. Thank you. Oh, yes, I was just handed this document this very instant. I may show this document, if this is necessary. I may ask some more questions then relating to this

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...to ask this question, could you please put it in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gladly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, can you see your name appearing on this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. On this document, Witness, do you see some typing, some words that can be read from right to left and left to right, basically at the bottom of this page? Witness, do you see that the words written on this document where written from left to right and from right to left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Do you mean at the very bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, that is precisely it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A matter in dispute. I expect --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. It is not. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know, I have to ask Mr. Ierace. I see the text going from right to left and from left to right

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That is not in dispute, Mr. President. It is simply what someone is seeing from the reverse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where it comes from is a different matter. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. Usher, would you be kind enough to hand me this document. Please give it back to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you have compared the two squares that appear in this document and they seem to be printed in reverse, one is the reverse of the other. I would like to draw your attention to one particular point.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, what I am trying to do right now is I am trying to compare. I withdraw this question. Since one portion of this copy is not produced in the original, I cannot ask the question that I wished to ask. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to ask that we place actually on the ELMO the picture that we have seen earlier bearing mark 2363. This is a document that I am handing to the usher right now, document P2363. Madam, do you see this picture and can we also place it on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. We are not in closed session at this moment. Because of the protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can become closed session or --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. That will not be necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please put the photo in front of the witness. It is for your protection, Mrs. AJ, that we don't want at this moment where to have any photographs on that machine so that anyone outside this courtroom could also see it. It is just a very short moment, Madam Registrar. It didn't. So we not need to give a decision for redaction. Just leave it in front of you. Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Terribly sorry, Mr. President. This technical detail completely escaped me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, we all remember that on this picture -- we will not place the picture on the ELMO for the above mentioned reasons -- but you have indicated with a cross a place which you have also indicated with the number one; do you see this mark that you yourself placed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes. This is what we call the shopping of Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am terribly sorry. Can you speak louder. I can't really hear well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Usher, would you please turn the volume up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you assist the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can you hear me, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, it is better. Thank you. Madam, I thought it under the cross with which you have indicated a number one, you meant to indicate a tall building; a high-rise, could you please answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes, it is a very tall building that we call the shopping in Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please take back this picture, Mr. Usher. Thank you very much. And give it back to the clerk. Thank you. I would have two more questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you have stated earlier -- can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: No, not very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you perhaps -- I will give you another headphone, Mrs. AJ. I hope that this is better. Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam, you have stated not long ago that you had a work obligation, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam, if I ask you the following question: Is it true to say that you were working for the army at the time; would you be able to answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You cannot answer or you were not working for the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: No, I was not. No, not a chance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam, one last question: When did you hand out the original documents to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yesterday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. But you had it during the interview of June of 2001, you were in possession of those documents in June of 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But you had these documents with you during the interview?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, that concludes cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Ierace

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just one matter. It relates to questions asked by Mr. Piletta-Zanin -- Ms. Pilipovic on page 79 of the transcript. Two questions and the answers commencing at line 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Madam, you were asked whether you saw anyone else at the time that you were shot, and in particular, you were told that in your statement to the investigators you had said that you noticed a person in sight. You then replied, "No, that is not what I said. Did you in fact say in your statement dated the 25th of June, 2001, these words, "I noticed that I was the only person in sight [Realtime transcript read in error "inside"] and things seemed very quiet"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Mrs. AJ, since the Judges have no further questions to you, this concludes your examination as a witness in this court. We want you to know that it is important for this Court to hear the testimony of the people who have been, at relevant times and at relevant places, that have been present and to hear the answer these witnesses give to the questions put by both the Prosecution and the Defence to these witnesses. So I thank you very much that you have come to The Hague because I am quite aware that it is a journey. And I wish you a safe journey home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just before you do the exhibits, may I make a correction to the transcript? In relation to the questions that I have just asked in re-examination, instead of the words "in sight," I think they appear instead as one word "inside," i-n-s-i-d-e. That is page 91, line 22, and page 92, line 2. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will just try to find it. Page 91, line 22, reads: "Re-examined by Mr. Ierace." I am looking off my laptop and that is -- yes, I think proper care will be taken of your remark. Then I think we have to deal with the documents. Madam Registrar, could you please assist us.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3679 under seal, pseudonym sheet; Exhibit P3263, photograph and signature sheet under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that the signature sheet is the back of the photograph, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3279Y under seal, 360-degree Quicktime movie; Exhibit P3280Y under seal, video; Exhibit P3282, medical documentation in B/C/S; Exhibit P3282.1, English translation, both under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I only rely on the first two pages on the original and the first two pages of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I just wanted those. So that would mean that from P3282, the Prosecution only tenders page 0211-5955, and same number but last digit "6" and the translation related to that. That is as far as the Prosecution is concerned. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have a remark that I have indeed just made. The Defence cannot accept to be supplied would a great number of exhibit for a single witness, exhibits which are practically all illegible. And we cannot accept not receiving legible copies before the actual testimony of the witness. And since we know that in June, year 2001, as we could see from the testimony of the witness, it has been almost a year since then, so the Prosecution was in a position to produce perfectly or sufficiently legible copies since the witness supplied such documents, such copies. We cannot accept being supplied with these documents just a few hours before the hearing, and the Prosecution has to comply with its basic obligation to disclose such documents to us. As far as these facts are concerned, the Defence considers that its rights were infringed, both in the case of this witness and the previous witness. The Defence is then required to prepare without having access to such important documents. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I first ask you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the Prosecution has tendered only the first two pages of P3282. Are these new documents -- I know that you were only provided with them yesterday. So would they have been legible enough as such?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for this question. Questioning a witness does not amount to questioning the witness only about only these two pages, these two documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am perfectly aware of that. I myself was -- this is a different issue than I am at this moment dealing with. It means, is last two digits 55 and 56 as they have been presented today by the Prosecutor, would they have been, well, acceptably legible?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would have to see them again, to go through them again, but to our mind -- yes, thank you. To our mind, it doesn't really change anything to the fact that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First I am putting a question to you, and whether it would change anything is a different matter. But I would like to know and the Chamber would like to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can make out some of the lines. I can read something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what you cannot read, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must notice with great deal of interest, Mr. President, and once again I must say that this is a typical example of what goes on. I must notice with a great deal of surprise that the entry date for this witness would have been the 27th of November, 1992 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I was talking about legibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I read so well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- must be in this document is fine, but I am just asking you now about legibility and which words or which parts you cannot read so that we can pay attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will answer immediately. I have some difficulties reading the second line and the third line of this text regarding the document ending with 55. But the date, the entry, the 27th of November, 1992 is perfectly clear and it completely contradicts all the other statements made by the witness. I read relatively well the line two, line two of the document 56, second line of document 56.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now you are commenting. Of course you are entirely free to make whatever -- to put whatever questions to witnesses or to experts and whether it contradicts other evidence. What I am concentrating about now is that you raise the issue of illegibility. I want to find what is illegible. You say the first two lines of the text and you are referring to, well, let's say to the bigger block of text which is in the bottom part, the lower half; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we are talking about the page ending with number 55, I said in fact, Mr. President, that the second and third line is, to my mind, not very legible. If we go to the second page of this document ending with numbers 56, I can say that I cannot read very clearly what is written in the first line, but I believe that for somebody who knows this, was a bigger expert in these matters, maybe they can read it better than I can

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is clear. Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I do understand that your objection goes further to the extent that other documents not tendered by the Prosecution were not legible either. I think they are attached to your "determination de la defense a redaction a la problematique des pieces illisible." So we can take notice of that. We also can now compare the quality of the documents that you have submitted to be provided to you, and the Prosecution could respond to that, if possible. We will give a decision on that in a later stage. I think we should first should consider the matter. Is there any other document? Since you want to question the witness about -- as a matter of fact, you questioned witness about the document with the numbers last two digits 57 and 58. Do you want to tender them or?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me please consult my colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me apologise to the interpreters' booth. Although I intended to stop at a quarter to 2.00, and we took five minutes more. I think it will be a matter of one, two, or three minutes. Would it be possible for you to proceed for these couple of minutes?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Absolutely, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we do not wish to add anything more. The answer is no. I think they are already an annex of our submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In order to avoid whatever misunderstanding, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you attach something to a submission to the Court, that does not mean that it is admitted into evidence and I perfectly, coming from a similar background, I perfectly understand that type of reason, that is, if it is in the file, it is something that the Chamber can take into consideration. But of course admitting into evidence is a different matter in the tradition from which most of the rules of this Court stem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President if my friend does not wish to tender those two pages, I propose to tender them. I would be grateful however if the pages attached to P3282 be tendered, rather than the ones that were shown to the witness because the ones which are part of P3282 are far more legible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think part of the evidence was just about whether it was legible or not. So therefore only the badly legible copies have been presented to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In that case, Mr. President, perhaps I should formally tender additionally to my earlier tender as part of P3282, those pages 5957 and 5958, regardless of whether Mr. Piletta-Zanin tenders the two pages which he showed to the witness

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we have then now in front of us the Prosecution tendering 55, 56, 57 and 58 and it being part of P3282 and the Prosecution -- and the Defence, if you want to tender it, then we have the same ERN numbers, but it would have a D number in front of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, then the difficulty would be the following: The difficulty we will tender will formally, or will not be the same document as the one stemming from the Prosecution. It is not the same document tendered by the Prosecution because we have it in a legible version so that things are clear. This is why I am saying this. Then we will photocopy them and hand them with your leave, Mr. President, either on Monday or at the end of the meeting Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I suggest to do is by way of exception, the numbers 57 and 58 will be taken from the attachment so that we are quite sure that that is the legibility and that as a matter of exception we will see whether we can have copies made, and then there would be a D number and it would be D --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that tender for the Prosecution includes the translation for those two pages as well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is one translation for 57 and 58 because there is no legibility problem and I don't see any difference in the translation. So tendering the translation, I think the Prosecution -- I am sorry. That is what happens if you go on too long. So the translation is just tendered by the Prosecution, not by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Mr. President. Thank you very much for this solution. We really appreciate this very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn not until tomorrow, but until next Monday at a quarter past 2.00, if I am correct, Madam Registrar, in this same courtroom. So we have the long afternoon session. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just one final matter. Given the requirement of seven days notice, I will confirm in writing this afternoon that we will call Robert Donia next Thursday. I think that allows seven clear days. In the meantime, if the Defence indicates to me in more detail the pages they are missing, then I would be happy to provide them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I wish everyone a good weekend. I wouldn't say a long weekend, but since some of us might see it fit to continue working also when we are not sitting. Until next Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
